items_missed: Never asked 'How are you today?' after the initial greeting
No full agenda statement with a time estimate ('takes about 10-15 minutes') or explicit 'sound good?' confirmation before diving into intake questions
Never asked about storage needs or storage stops
Skipped the 'pricing is super simple' opener before launching into rate breakdown
No Worries Damage Coverage (up to $2,000) never mentioned
Meet Your Mover program never mentioned
Only a partial no-hidden-fees pitch — covered no deposit/no cancellation fees, but never mentioned no fuel surcharge or no assembly fees
Gave only a high-end estimate figure with no stated low end, so no real time/cost range for the customer to anchor on
Misstated the transportation fee as the same as the hourly rate ($204 vs. $245), had to self-correct mid-explanation, creating confusion for the customer
Entire Save Your Ass prep speech skipped — no consolidation tips (toys, garden tools, drawers), no 'take a carload' tip, no sense-check close
Never asked 'any other questions before I let you go?'
Never gave office hours or how to reach the team with questions
Never used the customer's first name once during the call
No effective insurance explanation (No Worries coverage or 60c/lb baseline) tied to the pricing walkthrough
top_strength: Chris was methodical and patient through discovery, walking room-by-room (bedroom, living room, patio) and nailing down access details like elevator distance, TV sizes, and box count to build an accurate profile before quoting.
coaching_note: Build the three differentiators — No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, and On-Time Guarantee — into the pricing script before asking for the booking; none were mentioned here, so the customer walked away with a bare hourly rate and no reason Einstein beats a cheaper competitor on the next call he makes.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient throughout but transactional — heavy use of flat 'Okay' acknowledgments, no use of the customer's name, and no rapport-building beyond the task.
